title: California's HCAI notifies applicants that Funding Portal 1.0 applications were reachable through search engine links
date_note: Date of HCAI's notice letter (November 16, 2026), also the Reported Date on the California Attorney General's breach list. HCAI says it discovered the exposure on May 27, 2026; the register gives no breach date.
org: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)
geo_basis: agency address on the notice letter (2020 West El Camino Ave, Sacramento)
summary: California's HCAI says in a November 16 notice that on May 27, 2026 it found some grant, scholarship and loan applications in its Funding Portal 1.0 could be opened through search engine links, because of an MFA misconfiguration; HCAI says it was not a cyber attack. Applications may include names, ID numbers and, where supplied, Social Security numbers or medical information. HCAI reports no evidence of misuse.
plain: A California state health agency says grant, scholarship and loan applications in its online portal could be opened from search engine links because of a login setting mistake. It says there is no sign anyone misused the data.
exec: A state agency's portal settings left applications with ID and possibly Social Security numbers reachable from search engines.
action: HCAI's notice urges applicants to consider placing a fraud alert with the credit bureaus, review credit reports for unusual activity, and enroll in the Experian IdentityWorks monitoring it offers by February 28, 2027.
impact: Applicants who used Funding Portal 1.0 between 2017 and May 27, 2026; HCAI gives no number of people.

sources.name: HCAI Notice of Data Breach (sample letter filed with the California Attorney General)
California Attorney General breach register entry: Department of Health Care Access and Information

report.publisher: Department of Health Care Access and Information
key_findings: Some Funding Portal 1.0 applications could be accessed through search engine links because of an MFA misconfiguration, discovered May 27, 2026
HCAI says this was not a cyber attack and reports no evidence of misuse
Portal taken offline May 27 and restored May 29, 2026 after MFA settings were corrected
recommendations: Consider a fraud alert and review credit reports
Enroll in Experian IdentityWorks by February 28, 2027

validation.note: Primary source: HCAI's own notice letter, filed with the California Attorney General (register entry read; Reported Date 11/16/2026 from the Attorney General's breach list). No news coverage read.

evidence.quote: On May 27, 2026, HCAI discovered that some grant, scholarship, and loan applications submitted through our Funding Portal 1.0 could be accessed by certain search engine links.
Since you submitted an application in Funding Portal 1.0 between 2017 and May 27, 2026, your information may have been exposed.
Ensure that you enroll by February 28, 2027 (Your code will not work after this date.)

review.note: plain said 'old' applications; notice covers applications 2017 to May 27, 2026 (stronger than the source); removed. Date, MFA cause, not-a-cyber-attack wording, data types, offline/restored dates, Feb 28 2027 deadline and evidence quotes match the notice.
